name: Neck Curl
description: The neck curl is performed lying supine on a bench with the head extending off the edge, using a plate or neck harness to resist cervical flexion. The exercise targets the deep cervical flexors and sternocleidomastoid, building anterior neck strength and stability that supports the cervical spine under load. It is used by combat athletes, football players, and lifters seeking to strengthen the neck musculature for performance and injury prevention.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench with the head extending off one end. Hold a weight plate against the forehead with both hands, or use a neck harness. Begin with the head in a neutral or slightly extended position.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with no additional weight (bodyweight) or a very light plate (2.5-5 lbs). The neck musculature is not accustomed to direct loading and must be progressed extremely slowly.
steps: Step 1: Lie supine with the head off the bench edge, holding a plate to the forehead or wearing a neck harness.
Step 2: Begin from the neutral or slightly extended position.
Step 3: Curl the head forward, bringing the chin toward the chest (cervical flexion).
Step 4: Hold briefly at the top.
Step 5: Lower slowly and under full control back to the start.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using too heavy a weight before the neck is conditioned — build progressively over weeks
Jerking the head — movement must be slow and controlled
Performing this exercise if experiencing any neck pain or disc issues
safety_considerations: This exercise is contraindicated with any cervical disc pathology or acute neck pain
Progress load extremely slowly — the cervical spine is delicate
Always use a spotter or be conservative with plate placement
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: From neutral or slight extension to full cervical flexion (chin to chest).
coaching_cues: Build weeks of work before adding weight
